mainProblem.title: Persistent Headache
mainProblem.summary: The patient reports experiencing a persistent headache for four days.

importantFindings: Lab Findings: Platelet count flagged as low
aiSummary.clinicalSummary: A 30-year-old male presents with a persistent headache that has lasted for four days. A document review indicates a lab test showing a low platelet count. Complete vitals, past medical history, and specific headache location/intensity are currently unrecorded. Given the combination of a multi-day headache and low platelets, prompt clinician assessment is needed to determine the underlying cause and ensure patient safety.
whatCanBeDoneNow: Measure and record baseline vital signs including body temperature, blood pressure, pulse, and SpO2.
Advise the patient to rest comfortably in a quiet room and maintain adequate hydration.
Monitor closely for any emerging warning signs such as fever, neck stiffness, nausea, or visual changes.
redFlags: Documented low platelet count (risk of bleeding/underlying infection)
Assess for red flag symptoms: high fever, stiff neck, sudden severe pain, vision alterations, or confusion.

medicationSuggestions.name: Paracetamol
medicationSuggestions.reason: Symptomatic pain relief for headache; preferred over NSAIDs (like Aspirin/Ibuprofen) due to the low platelet count flag.
medicationSuggestions.safetyConsiderations: Do not administer NSAIDs owing to bleeding risk associated with low platelets. Confirm hepatic function and lack of allergies before use.

aiSummary.recommendedNextStep: Schedule a clinical consultation with a medical officer for complete vital assessment and further investigation of the low platelet count.

triage.reason: Four-day duration of headache paired with a lab finding of low platelet count warrants prompt medical evaluation to rule out acute febrile illnesses or hematological complications.
